discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard ΛCDM cosmological model

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe turned cosmology into a precision science. Bennett conceived and led the mission; Page led the design and calibration of the differential radiometers and the control of instrumental systematics; Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. Their all-sky maps of temperature and polarization anisotropies measured the acoustic peaks, the age, geometry and composition of the Universe to percent precision, detected early reionization through large-scale polarization, and showed a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum of primordial fluctuations with a small tilt, as inflation predicts. WMAP fixed the six-parameter ΛCDM model that every later probe, including Planck, galaxy surveys, baryon acoustic oscillations and the distance ladder, now tests. Its results have withstood two decades of independent scrutiny. Its open release of data, likelihoods and methods set the standard for how collaborative physics is shared, and its legacy frames today's search for new physics in cosmological tensions.
